cold-showers.claim: Do cold showers boost your immune system?

explanation.text: There is no clear evidence that cold showers strengthen immune function. A
found fewer self-reported days off work, but no significant reduction in illness days. A
found no significant immediate change in measured immune function after cold-water exposure. Those findings do not establish an immune-system boost.

sources.title: The Effect of Cold Showering on Health and Work: A Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.takeaway: Cold showering reduced self-reported sickness absence, but not illness days.

sources.title: Effects of cold-water immersion on health and wellbeing: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.takeaway: Pooled trials found no significant immediate immune-function effect.

cracking-knuckles.claim: Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis?

explanation.text: Studies have not found a link between habitual knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis. In a
, arthritis was similarly common in people who cracked their knuckles and those who did not. A
found no immediate swelling or loss of hand function after cracking. These studies are limited, so they cannot rule out every long-term effect.

sources.title: Knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis
sources.publisher: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine · 2011
sources.takeaway: Hand osteoarthritis prevalence was similar in habitual crackers and non-crackers.

sources.title: "Knuckle Cracking": Can Blinded Observers Detect Changes with Physical Examination and Sonography?
sources.takeaway: No immediate adverse examination findings were detected; long-term outcomes remain untested.
